artworks.title: Cyparissus
artworks.description: Vignali's Baroque canvas in the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Strasbourg shows the Cean youth mourning the tame stag he has accidentally slain — the grief Apollo will answer by turning him into the cypress, emblem of endless mourning.

artworks.title: Metamorphosis of Cyparissus (House of the Vettii)
artworks.description: A Pompeian fresco from the House of the Vettii stages Ovid's metamorphosis: Cyparissus beside the stag whose death will root him forever as the funeral cypress.

artworks.title: Apollo and Cyparissus
artworks.artist: Unknown (Dutch print; Metamorphoses of Ovid series)
artworks.description: A Dutch Metamorphoses engraving: Apollo with Cyparissus and the doomed stag — the pastoral friendship that ends when the youth's accidental shot becomes the aetiology of the cypress.

artworks.title: Cyparissus Changed into a Cypress
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum engraving of the climax Ovid names: Cyparissus transformed into the cypress tree, grief made evergreen — the reception image that keeps the Cean youth as a botanical myth.

popCulture.title: Cyparissus
popCulture.description: The youth who killed his tame stag and became the cypress remains Ovid's emblem of endless mourning — grief rooted as an evergreen.
